posts.author: JohnDoeGames
posts.body:
Spoiler:
Intro
Remember those challenges we did a few years ago? Where I came up with a random problem and we all came up with an event-only solution? That was fun, wasn't it? I thought so.
Back then, we treated it as a competition, with strict rules, and nothing to gain. And I think that is why it stopped. But the challenges were much more than a competition. They were great practice. And practicing on problems you would otherwise not encounter, is something I just love to do. So, I would like to challenge you all again.
This time, I will not give any hard rules. If the rules say you can't use a plugin, and you really need to create a little plugin to make your otherwise perfect solution come true, you won't be disqualified and there is no penalty. There is nothing to gain, and there is nothing to lose.
It is important that you use your own work, though. This has to be your solution completely, or else the whole practice is useless.
Spoiler:
Guidelines and How To Participate
Guidelines:
You must use any RPG maker you own
You can have to event the solution, you can not use plugins
You can use JavaScript in script calls, variables and conditions
Allowed art for tilesets and characters:
RTP (incl. character generator made)
Your own edits if necessary for your solution to work.
Explain what you've changed in your edits and why.
Allowed art for user interface:
RTP
Your own edits
Free community made assets from the forum (please provide link)
Explain the assets you use outside RTP. How and why do you use them?
To participate, you have to have to:
Post screenshots of your full event in a reply (see example 1)
Explain what happens in those screenshots
Quote your script calls (see example 2)
Explain your code
Be open to feedback, positive and negative
Clearly mention WHICH challenge you apply to.
Example 1 (Taken from
my tutorial
)
Example 2 (Quoted from the same tutorial)

Click to expand...
I challenge you to make eventing-only solutions to random problems. For example "Create a lockpicking system with a difficulty level", which was the original problem that sparked the challenges years ago, by the way.
Challenges will run forever.
There is no deadline!
They are not a competition. You simply share your solution, compare them with other solutions and see what people have to say about yours. The goal is not to win, but to practice, to teach and to learn.
We all deal with those problems in a different way. Some solutions are better than others. But often 2 solutions are completely different and both get the job done perfectly well. And that is where it gets interesting.
Sometimes you think you have a genius idea, and then it turns out you've been overthinking it this whole time, when you see how other made it. Or you think you just made something basic and easy, and then it turns out your had that genius idea no-one else has thought of.
And if you fail the challenge? Did you have this amazing plan, but can't figure out why it doesn't work? Send in your solution in anyway! Maybe others can see what is wrong with your plan. Sometimes you just need a fresh pair of eyes.
Challenge 1: Status bars
Started: December 2024
Spoiler:
Details
Use events to create status bars on your map.
You choose how the how this event is triggered to update the bars.
Goals:
Show an accurate bar for HP, MP and TP of the party leader when on the map.
Show a background behind the bars (optionally with a border a round the bars)
Bonus goals:
Show the right portrait next to the bars
Repeat the whole process for 1, 2 or even 3 followers. (Or 12, if you're ambitious.)
Super bonus goal:
Add state icons to the right portraits.
Why not start of with an easy one?
Nah, I know this is a challenge, but if I can do it, so can you. And yes, I'll share my solution, too. I enjoyed working on mine, so I hope even though it isn't an easy one to start with, it is at least a fun one to work on.

My best guess is you could "solve" it using variables and pictures, but in no way would the bars be "accurate" since you'd need a new picture for basically every single pixel and then do a bunch of math.

posts.author: JohnDoeGames
posts.body:
Here is my entry for
Challenge 1: Status bars
So far I focused on 1 character, and I ignored states.
Here is how I did it:
First I showed the background, which is a single image, that covers the whole screen. So, we place it at coordinates 0, 0.
The second image is the player image. This can be more dynamic, when the player has the option to switch party leaders, but I choose to make it for a game where only 1 character is playable, so there was no need for that. (I plan to do this later, just like the states.)
The third command is the interesting one... The script call.
This call will do the following, line by line:
This looks for the actor ID of the party leader.
This looks for the current HP in %
This looks for the current MP in %
This looks for the current TP (Since max is 100, it is always in %)
This places the HP bar
This places the MP bar
This places the TP bar
So, basically what happens is: I show 3 images (one for each bar), and the height of those images are always 100%, but the width in % is equal to the HP, MP or TP in %.
When you have 30%, the bar for HP is only 30% wide, and therefor 70% empty.
This is triggered with a parallel common event that loops 6 times per second. I also trigger it each time a player gets damage on the map (like when bitten by a bat outside of battle), to prevent the bar updating a fraction of a second later. The only reason I made it also parallel is to update it after healing in the main menu (by using a skill or a potion). Of course, I could also have the skill and the potion trigger this common event. Then I don't need a parallel trigger at all.
Here is a the code, so you can copy it over and re-use it if you like:
JavaScript:
var ID = $gameParty.leader().actorId();
var HP = $gameActors.actor(ID).hp * 100 / $gameActors.actor(ID).mhp;
var MP = $gameActors.actor(ID).mp * 100 / $gameActors.actor(ID).mmp;
var TP = $gameActors.actor(ID).tp;
$gameScreen.showPicture(93, 'Bar_HP', 0, 480, 48,  HP, 100, 255, 0);
$gameScreen.showPicture(94, 'Bar_MP', 0, 480, 64,  MP, 100, 255, 0);
$gameScreen.showPicture(95, 'Bar_TP', 0, 480, 80,  TP, 100, 255, 0);
And here are the graphics I used from the pictures folder:
You can use everything in your project if you like. Just, replace the face image.
If you want to use my interface, you can scale the face of your party leader to 50% and then crop it into a perfect circle. Place that in the exact center of a 144x144 image, and name it "Face.png". Now my system should work with your game.
Easy peasy right? And if you know how to do a bit of editing, you can make very pretty and cute interfaces surrounding your portait and status bars.

If you have a simple bar that can extend 'indefinitely' (such as a vertical gradient on a horizontal bar or just a white line), you could probably just use Width in Move Picture to 'shrink' the bar inside the border.
